title: Decide when the reasoning loop may stop
description: Generate candidates, run the task-appropriate checker, and commit to accept, continue, or escalate. Agreement and evidence are deliberately separated.

scenarios.label: Executable patch
scenarios.detail: A code change has a deterministic behavior test.

checker.label: Contract tests
checker.result: Patch A passes; Patch B violates the edge-case contract.

scenarios.escalation: Send the failing trace and candidate diff to the code owner.
scenarios.lesson: One passing candidate plus an objective check can justify stopping; more samples are not automatically better.

scenarios.label: Repeated unsupported claim
scenarios.detail: Several candidates agree, but truth lives in an external policy record.

checker.label: Versioned policy lookup
checker.result: The current approved record states 30 days; the majority answer is unsupported.

scenarios.escalation: Route the source conflict to the policy owner instead of choosing by vote.
scenarios.lesson: Agreement measures repetition. An authoritative source can overturn a confident majority.

scenarios.label: High-impact architecture trade-off
scenarios.detail: Several designs are plausible and no automatic checker captures ownership or risk appetite.

candidates.summary: Adds an outbox and bounded queue

checker.label: Automatic verifier
checker.result: No objective checker can decide the business consistency and recovery trade-off.

scenarios.escalation: Present assumptions, alternatives, failure modes, and cost to the accountable architecture owner.
scenarios.lesson: More reasoning can clarify options, but it cannot manufacture the authority required to commit the trade-off.
